summary: E. H. Rogers worked in linguistics and Indology. He served as Head Master at The Lawrence School, Sanawar, in 1858 and became a Sub-Inspector for Army Schools in 1861.
E. M. Hare worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He was educated at Stamford School from circa 1905 to 1911 and studied under Frank Lee Woodward from circa 1920 to 1935.

E. Michael Mendelson was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at King's College, Cambridge (~1946–1949), the University of Chicago (~1949–1951), and the University of Paris (~1951–1957). He also taught Jane Bunnag.

E. R. Sreekrishna Sarma was an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Marburg under Johannes Nobel (~1951–1954). He held a post at Sri Venkateswara University from circa 1959 to 1982.

Indologist E. Sherman Oakley studied at the University of Glasgow, Airedale Independent College, and the University of Allahabad. He joined the London Missionary Society in 1888 and served as Principal of Ramsay College from circa 1908 to 1916.

E. W. Adikaram studied at Wesley College, University of Colombo, SOAS, and the University of London, earning a PhD under William Stede. In 1934, the Buddhist studies scholar served as principal at Ananda Sastralaya, Kotte.

Indologist and linguist Ebbe Oskar Tuneld studied at Lund, Berlin, Leipzig, Göttingen, and Paris under Flensburg, Oldenberg, Meillet, and Lévi. He became PD of Indology in 1915 and Professor in 1923 at Lund University.

Ebenezer Burgess studied at Amherst College from circa 1827 to 1831 and at Andover Theological Seminary from circa 1834 to 1837. He served as a missionary for the American Board of Commissioners for Foreign Missions from 1839 to 1854.

Ebenezer Charles Bethlehem Hallam, who worked in Indology and linguistics, was educated at King Edward's School, Birmingham, and Toronto Normal School. He served as a missionary with the American Free Baptist Mission and the Baptist Missionary Society.

Eberhard Fischer is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Basel (~1960–1965). He served as Direktor of Museum Rietberg (1972–1998) and Secretary General of the Swiss-Liechtenstein Foundation for Archaeological Research Abroad.

Historian Eberhard Gothein studied at Breslau under Wilhelm Dilthey and at Heidelberg. He was Professor of Nationalökonomie at Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (1884–1890), the University of Bonn (1890–1905), and Heidelberg University (1905).

Eberhard Sandschneider studied at Saarland University, completing his PhD around 1986. A sinologist, he served as Professor at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (1995–1998), Director at Free University of Berlin (1999–2001), and Otto-Wolff-Direktor at the DGAP (2003–2016).

Linguist Eberhard Schrader studied under Heinrich Ewald at the University of Göttingen (~1856–1860). He held posts at the universities of Zurich, Giessen, and Jena before serving as Professor at Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1875 to 1908.

Indology and philosophy scholar Edeltraud Harzer studied at Charles University, the University of Washington, and under Shrinarayan Mishra and Ram Shankar Bhattacharya. She held appointments at Indiana, Washington, Puget Sound, Stanford, Leiden, and Texas at Austin.

Linguist Edgar Howard Sturtevant studied at Illinois College, Indiana University, and the University of Chicago under Carl Darling Buck. He taught at Indiana, Maryville, Missouri, and Columbia, before serving as Assistant Professor at Yale from 1923 to 1943.

Linguist and Indologist Edgar Polomé studied at Université libre de Bruxelles and Université catholique de Louvain under Étienne Lamotte. He was Professor of Linguistics at the University of Lubumbashi (1956–1960) and Director at UT Austin (1961–1997).

Edgar Thurston studied at Eton College and King's College London. He served as Superintendent of the Government Museum, Chennai (1885–1908), lecturer at Madras Medical College (~1885–1908), and Superintendent of Ethnography for the Madras Presidency in 1901.

Edgard Blochet studied under James Darmesteter at the EPHE and INALCO. Working in Iranian and central Asian religious studies, he taught at the EPHE (1895–1901) and served as a librarian at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1895–1935).

Edith Frances Claflin, a scholar of linguistics and Indology, studied at Radcliffe College (B.A.) and Bryn Mawr College (A.M., Ph.D.). She led Choate Rosemary Hall's Greek Department (1916–1933) and lectured at Barnard College (1936–1945).
Edith Ludowyk-Gyömrői was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied under G. P. Malalasekera at the University of Ceylon, where she completed her Ph.D. between circa 1939 and 1944.
